resolutions.researcher_notes: Status=operating confirmed by two independent sources. Saudipedia: 'Gas production began in October 2015 to supply the Wasit Gas Plant, and its production rate reached two billion ft3 of non-associated gas per day.' Offshore-technology (Al Wasit Gas Program): Wasit CPF processing 2.5 bcf/d of non-associated Hasbah/Arabiyah gas, brought onstream 2015-16. Field/plant clearly in production => operating. Prior al-jazirah ref was dead.

Stated Capacity=1.00 MMcf/d is a placeholder that NO source supports and that contradicts reality. Hasbah field feeds Wasit at ~2 billion cf/d (Saudipedia); Wasit plant designed for 2.5 billion scf/d of sour Hasbah+Arabiyah gas (offshore-technology). A 1 MMcf/d pipeline throughput is three orders of magnitude too small. Flag for Update: replace placeholder or blank. No ref added for the false value.

Stated LengthKnown=80 km has no corroborating source. Published Hasbah->Wasit figures are all different: offshore-technology (Al Wasit) gives a 260 km 36in offshore export pipeline to the CPF plus a 120 km onshore line; the Hasbah field lies ~150 km NE of Jubail; the Hasbah expansion pipelines are 120 km and 126 km carbon-steel sections (36in). None equals 80 km. Could not locate any source stating 80 km, so left UNRESOLVED and flagged the discrepancy for Update to reconcile.

FuelSource=Hasbah Gas Field confirmed by two independent sources. Saudipedia: gas produced from the Hasbah field platforms is transported via 36in pipelines to the Wasit Gas Plant. Offshore-technology (Hasbah Gas Field Expansion): non-associated gas from the offshore Hasbah field exported to Wasit gas plant through 36in-diameter pipeline. Both name Hasbah as the source field.

Status=operating. OGJ (Mar 2016): 'Saudi Aramco has commissioned offshore Hasbah natural gas field'; gas flows 'to the Wasit gas plant' via 'twin 36-in. trunklines' — confirms the export line is live. Offshore-technology independently documents the Hasbah->Wasit 36in export pipeline with Wasit plant onstream Oct 2015 / full capacity 2016. Two independent origins both support operating. Dead al-jazirah.com original replaced.

CONTRADICTION / placeholder: GEM value Capacity=1.00 MMcf/d is a placeholder, not a real throughput and no source can support it. Real figures: OGJ and offshore-technology give combined Hasbah+Arabiyah capacity of 2.5 bscfd to Wasit via twin 36-in trunklines; Hasbah field alone ~350 MMscfd (initial) / up to ~1.3 bscfd. A per-segment 'Pipeline 2' capacity of 1.00 MMcf/d is not documented anywhere. Left UNRESOLVED — recommend Update replace the placeholder or blank it rather than add a ref to an unsupported value.

No independent source states 80 km for a Hasbah->Wasit segment. Published figures: offshore-technology/offshore-mag give a 260 km 36in offshore export trunkline connecting both fields (150 km NE of Jubail) plus a 120 km onshore line; expansion lines (120 km + 126 km carbon steel) go to Fadhili, not Wasit. The 80 km appears to be GEM's own segmentation of 'Hasbah-Wasit Gas Pipelines' (Pipeline 2) and cannot be corroborated to a specific published length. Left UNRESOLVED — flag the 80 km as unverified segmentation.

FuelSource=Hasbah Gas Field. OGJ: production carried 'from the fields to the Wasit gas plant', explicitly naming Hasbah. Offshore-technology: 'The gas produced from the [Hasbah] field is transported to tie-in platforms and then exported to the Wasit gas plant through a 36in-diameter pipeline.' Two independent sources confirm Hasbah field is the upstream source. Dead aramco.com/ar original replaced.

Status 'operating' is inferred, not literal (per confidence_tiers guidance). No independent source names 'Abu Ali-Berri gas pipeline' specifically; the specific line traces only to the dead steel-network.com Arabic article (cite 3 on gem.wiki, not in Wayback) and OPEC ASB aggregates. Both endpoints are documented operating facilities: Saudipedia says Berri Gas Plant has operated since 1977 as part of Aramco's main gas network; nsenergybusiness confirms the existing Abu Ali GOSP facility and that Saudi Aramco owns and operates the Berri field (in production 4+ decades). Operating status of the connecting gas line is a reasonable contextual inference, not a directly-sourced fact.

Fuel=Gas well supported: Saudipedia describes Berri Gas Plant as a facility within Saudi Aramco's main gas network that processes gas and supplies natural gas to the Master Gas System. The Abu Ali-Berri line is a gas pipeline feeding the Berri Gas Plant, so Gas is consistent. One strong source (medium).

StartYear1=2008 could not be independently verified. The only source for 2008 is the dead steel-network.com Arabic article (gem.wiki cite 3), which is not archived in Wayback and returns no snapshot. The nearby Khursaniyah gas program / Abu Ali GOSP came online ~Dec 2007-2008, which makes a 2008 start plausible, but no source ties a 2008 in-service date to this specific Abu Ali-Berri gas line. OPEC ASB 2011/2012 (gem cites 1,2) are national aggregate statistics that do not document individual pipeline start years. Not fabricating a ref; UNRESOLVED.

LengthKnown=44 km could not be independently verified. The 44 km (and 30-inch diameter) figures trace solely to the dead steel-network.com Arabic article (gem.wiki cite 3), unarchived in Wayback. No independent trade/technical source (Aramco, MEED, OGJ, nsenergybusiness, Saipem) states a length for this line. UNRESOLVED.

FuelSource=Abu Ali Island partially supported: nsenergybusiness documents the existing Abu Ali GOSP facility (a Saudi Aramco gas-oil separation plant on Abu Ali Island near Jubail) that separates associated gas, consistent with Abu Ali Island being the upstream/source end of a gas line to Berri. The source confirms Abu Ali Island is a real Aramco hydrocarbon-processing point but does not explicitly name it as this pipeline's fuel source. Low tier.

Location values well corroborated by two independent sources. Saudipedia places the Berri Gas Plant in al-Jubayl (Al Jubail) Industrial City, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. nsenergybusiness places the Berri field production/processing facilities and the Abu Ali GOSP in Jubail, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. Both endpoints (Abu Ali Island start, Berri Gas Plant end at Al Jubail) sit in the Eastern Province. Supports EndLocation=Berri Gas Plant, EndPrefecture=Al Jubail, Start/End State=Eastern Province, Country=Saudi Arabia.

Value = operating. The Abu Ali-Berri gas line is part of Saudi Aramco's Abu Ali Island gas/crude processing system (Khursaniyah-Abu Ali-Berri corridor), which is an active, in-service facility. NS Energy (Berri Oil Field Expansion) and MEtenders both describe the existing, operating Abu Ali gas plant and its Khursaniyah/Juaymah pipeline connections as pre-existing infrastructure being expanded (2019-2024 Berri Increment), confirming the base system is operating. Two independent trade sources; both verified live and contain 'Abu Ali'. Dead original ref (steel-network.com Arabic Jubail-projects article) replaced. No contradiction to 'operating'.

Value = StartYear1 2008. The pipeline came onstream as part of Saudi Aramco's Khursaniyah oil & gas program (which built the Abu Ali Island processing plant plus its connecting gas/oil pipelines). Offshore Technology (construction from Sept 2005; gas program completion 2007-early 2008) and Oil & Gas Journal (Aramco megaprojects, Khursaniyah, 2008 completion) independently place the Khursaniyah/Abu Ali facilities and their pipelines onstream in 2008; both verified live and contain '2008' + 'Khursaniyah'. CAVEAT: neither source names the 'Abu Ali-Berri' gas line individually — corroboration is at the program level (the system these lines belong to), so tier=medium rather than high. No source contradicts 2008; the OPEC ASB seed cites (2011/2012 pipeline tables) are now paywalled/inaccessible and could not be verified.

The Madrakah–Al Hawiyah line is Aramco's 'free-flow' pipeline, built to bridge gas supply from the Madrakah/Haradh field area to the Hawiyah gas plant until the Haradh & Hawiyah compression plants came online (~2021). Mubasher (republishing the Jan 2018 Aramco release) reports construction/launch in 2018; OGJ (Dec 2017 contract award) describes the 450-km free-flow network. Status=operating is inferred from the 2018 launch with no later cancellation/idling reported. Note: offshore-technology labels the broader Haradh–Hawiyah compression project 'expected to commence operations in 2024' — that refers to the compression plants, not this free-flow pipeline.

ConstructionYear=2018 supported: OGJ reports the EPC contract (China Petroleum Pipelines, lump-sum) was signed Dec 2017 with the 450-km network to be installed 'by early 2019'; Mubasher (Aramco Jan 2018 release, token '2018' present) reports work launched/underway in 2018. So construction began 2018 — consistent with the stated value. Award-to-completion window 2017→2019.

Capacity=290 MMcf/d well corroborated: OGJ states the free-flow pipeline allows 'free flowing 290 MMscfd of gas from Haradh field to the Hawiyah gas plant'; Mubasher (token '290' present) reports the same 290 MMscfd. OGJ (independent editorial, Dec 2017 contract) and the Aramco-sourced Jan 2018 release are separate publications, both giving 290. MMscfd == MMcf/d, matches units.

Length=450 km strongly corroborated across three independent sources: OGJ ('installing a 450-km pipeline network'), offshore-technology/GlobalData ('450km-long', max diameter 36 in), and Mubasher (token '450' present). METenders (Package 5) also cites 450 km.

FuelSource=Madrakah supported: Mubasher (Aramco release, token 'Madrakah' present) names the source as Madrakah; METenders describes the scope as 'remote headers in the Midrakah fields' (Midrakah == Madrakah/مدركة). OGJ instead names 'Haradh field' generically — Madrakah/Midrakah is the specific field area within the Haradh gas development, so the sources are consistent rather than conflicting.

Endpoints Madrakah -> Al Hawiyah are confirmed (Mubasher names Madrakah and Al Hawiyah; OGJ says 'from Haradh field to the Hawiyah gas plant'). VALUE CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: GEM lists StartState/Province and EndState/Province = 'Makkah', but every source places both the Madrakah/Haradh field area and the Hawiyah gas plant in the Eastern Province (near Haradh), NOT Makkah province. The Makkah-province attribution appears to be a GEM error — likely a confusion with the separate town of Al Madrakah in Makkah region. Endpoints supported; province not supported.

VALUE CONTRADICTION / OVERATTRIBUTION TO FLAG: GEM records SegmentCost = USD 4.5 billion for this pipeline. OGJ (and the underlying Aramco Dec 2017 announcement) states the $4.5 billion covers EIGHT separate agreements across multiple megaprojects (the Haradh & Hawiyah gas development, compression plants, drilling, etc.), of which the free-flow pipeline is only ONE component. Attributing the full $4.5B to this single pipeline is an overstatement; the pipeline's standalone cost is not separately disclosed. Ref supports the $4.5B figure only in its true multi-project context.

Status=operating is supported: Aramco announced (Feb/Mar 2026) that Tanajib Gas Plant commenced operations in December 2025, coinciding with first production from the Marjan crude oil increment (the field these GOSP-4 trunk lines serve). Both cited trade outlets report Marjan increment onstream Dec 2025, so 'operating' holds today (2026-07). Marked independent=false because both trace to the same Aramco announcement; the underlying startup fact is well established. NOTE: the offshore platform delivered/sailed away from China in Aug 2024 was fabrication delivery, not operational start.

Fuel=Gas confirmed: Marjan Package 4 EPCI scope is explicitly 'offshore gas facilities and pipelines' (Aramco Marjan Increment gas facilities package). Two independent editorial outlets (Offshore Energy; NS Energy) both describe the gas facilities/pipelines. Supports Gas.

PipelineType=transmission is inferred, not literal: the scope is 'subsea trunk lines and in-field pipelines' (330 mi / 540 km). 'Trunk lines' = transmission-class carriage; both independent sources describe subsea trunk lines. Medium because 'transmission' is a classification inferred from the trunk-line description, not a stated term.

ConstructionYear=2019 supported: Aramco awarded the Marjan Package 4 offshore gas facilities/pipelines EPCI to McDermott/COOEC in July 2019, with the engineering phase scheduled to begin Q3 2019 (fabrication Q1 2020). Two independent outlets (Offshore Energy 2019-07-10; SaudiGulf Projects 2019-07) date the award/mobilization to 2019. Minor caveat: physical fabrication of the pipelines began early 2020; GEM anchors ConstructionYear to the 2019 award/engineering start.

VALUE CONTRADICTION — StartYear1=2024 is not supported by any source and appears wrong. The Aug 2024 event was fabrication delivery/sail-away of the GOSP-4 platform from China (per ecns.cn), not operational start. Aramco's own announcement states the Marjan crude oil increment served by these trunk lines reached FIRST PRODUCTION in December 2025 (Tanajib startup coincided with Marjan increment onstream); Zawya project updates through 2025 forecast onstream 'by 2025', never 2024. Recommend correcting StartYear1 to 2025 (Dec 2025). No source supports 2024 as the startup year, so left UNRESOLVED rather than back-filling a ref to a value that is likely incorrect.

LengthKnown=330 mi confirmed verbatim: Package 4 scope includes 'subsea trunk lines and in-field pipelines in excess of 330 miles (540 kilometers)'. Three sources carry the figure (McDermott PR via PR Newswire; plus two independent editorial outlets, Offshore Energy and NS Energy). Caveat worth noting: 330 mi is the TOTAL of all subsea trunk + in-field pipelines in the package, not necessarily a single point-to-point trunk length — but it is the sourced basis for GEM's LengthKnown.

Status 'operating' is inferred, not literal. ecns.cn (Aug 13 2024) reports the offshore GOSP platform for the Marjan field was delivered/completed after a 34-month build and will let the field ramp up output, transporting 7.4 bcm of gas annually + crude for Aramco -> operating by context. offshore-technology describes the same GOSP-4 expansion as commissioned (it says 2025). Minor date discrepancy: ecns implies 2024 delivery, offshore-technology says commissioned 2025 (see Start note). Both independent (Chinese state media vs UK trade site), both confirm the plant/pipelines reached completion, supporting 'operating'.

Fuel = Gas well supported. offshore-energy: Package 4 is EPCI of 'offshore gas facilities and pipelines' for the Marjan Increment. nsenergybusiness: GOSP-4 designed to handle ~750 Mscfd of gas with associated subsea gas infrastructure. Two independent trade sources.

PipelineType 'transmission' inferred from scope: offshore-energy describes 'subsea trunk lines and in-field pipelines' (trunk lines = transmission); nsenergybusiness describes subsea trunk/export pipelines carrying field production to shore. No source uses the literal word 'transmission', but trunk-line + field-to-shore role supports it. Two independent sources.

ConstructionYear 2019 = year Aramco awarded the Package 4 EPCI contract to McDermott (offshore-energy dated 2019-07-10; argaam Saudi-market report on the $4.5b Marjan package awards, 2019). Note: the same offshore-energy article puts actual fabrication at Q1 2020 through Q4 2022, so 2019 reflects award/EPCI kickoff rather than physical construction start; flagged but the 2019 stamp is supported by two independent sources.

StartYear1 2024 supported by 2024 completion/delivery of the Marjan GOSP offshore platform: ecns.cn (Aug 13 2024, platform delivered, field to ramp up output). china.aramco (Aramco's own release on completing fabrication of the platform in China, 2024) cited via Wayback because the live page timed out; Wayback snapshot verified OK/200 with 'Marjan' present. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: offshore-technology says the expansion was commissioned 2025, so first gas/start could be 2024 (platform delivered) or 2025 (commissioning) - value 2024 is defensible but not unanimous.

The 62 mi (~100 km) figure appears to trace to a 36-in subsea OIL trunk line, not a gas pipeline, and no independent source states 62 mi for a gas line. Possible oil/gas conflation - value left UNRESOLVED and flagged for review.

Matches StartState/Province 'Arabian Gulf', StartPrefecture/District 'Eastern Coast', country Saudi Arabia. Two independent sources.

This is a segment of Saudi Aramco's UBTG (Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas) system feeding Ju'aymah, part of the Master Gas System. Fluor's completed Saudi Aramco Gas Program EPC page and the OGN Master Gas System feature both describe this gas gathering/processing/trunkline network across Shedgum, Uthmaniyah, Ju'aymah, Berri and Jubail as built and in operation. Neither names this exact GEM segment, but both confirm the UBTG/MGS gas system is operating. Seed OPEC ASB citations are country-level statistics and do not support a segment status; not cited.

Fuel=Gas is well supported: Fluor describes this as a gas gathering and processing system (>3 bcf/d sour gas feed producing sweet dry gas), and OGN describes the Master Gas System distributing sales/dry gas. The UBTG-to-Ju'aymah lines are dry-gas / NGL trunklines of the gas program. Two independent sources agree it is gas infrastructure.
